subject.title: [Bug]: Discord sessions persist per-session exec directives, causing allowlist mode to behave unexpectedly after config changes

question: Should stored per-session `/exec` values remain higher-precedence persistent session defaults, or should global exec-policy changes automatically tighten existing Discord sessions?
rationale: Both directions affect command-execution security posture and compatibility: current docs support persistent session defaults, while the report shows that persistence can surprise operators after a global policy change.

options.title: Preserve Overrides With Reset
options.body: Keep documented persistent session overrides, but add/clarify operator audit, Doctor, or reset guidance for clearing stale exec fields after policy changes.

options.title: Make Channel Exec Ephemeral
options.body: Stop persisting channel-origin exec directives or clear them on restart/config generation so global policy automatically regains control.

options.title: Global Policy Wins
options.body: Change resolver precedence so global or agent exec policy can tighten stored session exec values, accepting the compatibility break for prior session defaults.

recommendation.title: Preserve Overrides With Reset
recommendation.body: Keep documented persistent session overrides, but add/clarify operator audit, Doctor, or reset guidance for clearing stale exec fields after policy changes.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent exec-policy resolver history makes this the best available routing owner for the precedence decision.
